records.source: וַיְהִ֞י בְּבֹ֨א דָוִ֧ד וַאֲנָשָׁ֛יו צִֽקְלַ֖ג בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י וַעֲמָלֵקִ֣י פָֽשְׁט֗וּ אֶל־נֶ֨גֶב֙ וְאֶל־צִ֣קְלַ֔ג וַיַּכּוּ֙ אֶת־צִ֣קְלַ֔ג וַיִּשְׂרְפ֥וּ אֹתָ֖הּ בָּאֵֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: And it was when came David and his men [to] Ziklag on the day the third, and [the] Amalekites had raided against [the] Negev and against Ziklag, and they had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire.
pieces: On the third day David and his men reached Ziklag. The Amalekites had raided the Negev and Ziklag. They had attacked Ziklag and burned it down.

L.1: And it happened, when David and his men came to Ziklag on the third day, [that the] Amalekites had made a raid on the Negev and on Ziklag, and they had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire.

R.1: On the third day after they left the Philistine army, David and his men got back to Ziklag. While they were away, the Amalekites had made a raid on the Negev, the dry land in the south. They had attacked Ziklag and burned it down.

decisions.choice: Ziklag on the third day: David's town, reached on the third day after he left the Philistine army
decisions.reason: Achish king of Gath had given Ziklag to David (27:6). The Philistine commanders had sent David away from their army at Aphek, and he left early in the morning to go back to the land of the Philistines (29:10-11). "The third day" counts from that departure; the march south to Ziklag was a long one.

decisions.choice: the Amalekites had raided the Negev: a sudden raid on the dry south country
decisions.reason: The verb means to dash out and strip a place, the word used of David's own raids on the Amalekites and their neighbors (27:8). The Negev is the dry southern land of Judah and the Philistine border. While David and the Philistine army were away in the north, the south lay open.

decisions.choice: had raided ... had struck ... had burned: things that happened before David arrived
decisions.reason: The verse opens with David's arrival and then tells, in the past, what the Amalekites had already done while he was gone. Verse 3 shows what David found.

decisions.choice: after they left the Philistine army; the dry land in the south
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the third day" counts from (m1) and explains the place name Negev once.

records.heading: The Amalekites raid Ziklag

records.source: וַיִּשְׁבּ֨וּ אֶת־הַנָּשִׁ֤ים אֲשֶׁר־בָּהּ֙ מִקָּטֹ֣ן וְעַד־גָּד֔וֹל לֹ֥א הֵמִ֖יתוּ אִ֑ישׁ וַיִּֽנְהֲג֔וּ וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ לְדַרְכָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And they had taken captive the women who [were] in it, from small and unto great; not they had killed anyone, and they had driven [them] off and gone on their way.
pieces: They had taken captive the women who were there, young and old alike. They had killed no one, but had carried them all off and gone on their way.

L.2: And they had taken captive the women who [were] in it, from small to great. They had not killed anyone, but they had driven [them] off and gone on their way.

R.2: They had captured the women and everyone else in the town, young and old. They did not kill anyone. They took them all away with them.

decisions.choice: from small to great: all of them, young and old
decisions.reason: The pair "small ... great" means everyone, whatever their age or rank (5:9; 30:19). Verse 3 shows that the captives were the men's wives, sons and daughters: the fighting men were all away with David.

decisions.choice: they killed no one, but drove them off: the captives were taken alive
decisions.reason: The Amalekites took people as plunder, to keep or sell as slaves. David had done the opposite on his raids, leaving no one alive (27:9, 11). The fact that the captives were alive makes the rescue possible.

decisions.choice: drove off: led away like a herd
decisions.reason: The verb is used for driving animals (verse 20) and for leading captives away (Genesis 31:26).

decisions.choice: the women and everyone else in the town
decisions.reason: Readable names the children as well, as verse 3 does, so that the reader is not left thinking only the women were taken.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֨א דָוִ֤ד וַֽאֲנָשָׁיו֙ אֶל־הָעִ֔יר וְהִנֵּ֥ה שְׂרוּפָ֖ה בָּאֵ֑שׁ וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֛ם וּבְנֵיהֶ֥ם וּבְנֹתֵיהֶ֖ם נִשְׁבּֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And came David and his men to the city, and there! [it was] burned with fire, and their wives and their sons and their daughters had been taken captive.
pieces: When David and his men came to the town, they found it burned down, and their wives, sons and daughters taken captive.

L.3: And David and his men came to the town, and look, [it was] burned with fire, and their wives and their sons and their daughters had been taken captive.

R.3: When David and his men got to the town, they saw that it had been burned. Their wives, sons and daughters had been taken away as prisoners.

decisions.choice: and look, burned: the scene as the men saw it on arrival
decisions.reason: The word often rendered "behold" moves the telling to what the arriving men saw with their own eyes: smoke and ruins and empty houses.

decisions.choice: the city: Ziklag, a small town
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for "city" covers any settlement with houses, walled or not. Here it is Ziklag (verse 1).

decisions.choice: they found / they saw
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "look" into a verb of seeing, which is what it marks (m1).

records.source: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א דָוִ֜ד וְהָעָ֧ם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֛וֹ אֶת־קוֹלָ֖ם וַיִּבְכּ֑וּ עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֧ר אֵין־בָּהֶ֛ם כֹּ֖חַ לִבְכּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And lifted up David and the people who [were] with him their voice and they wept, until that there was not in them strength to weep.
pieces: David and the troops with him wept aloud until they had no strength left to weep.

L.4: And David and the people who [were] with him lifted up their voice and wept, until there was no strength in them to weep.

R.4: David and his soldiers cried out loud until they were too weak to cry anymore.

decisions.choice: lifted up their voice and wept: wept aloud
decisions.reason: The phrase describes open, loud mourning (11:4; Genesis 27:38; Judges 2:4).

decisions.choice: the people: David's fighting men
decisions.reason: The people "with him" are the 600 men who followed David (verse 9; 27:2).

decisions.choice: troops (Balanced), soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: "The people" here are an army in the field, so Balanced says "troops" and Readable "soldiers", as elsewhere in 1 Samuel.

records.source: וּשְׁתֵּ֥י נְשֵֽׁי־דָוִ֖ד נִשְׁבּ֑וּ אֲחִינֹ֨עַם֙ הַיִּזְרְעֵלִ֔ית וַאֲבִיגַ֕יִל אֵ֖שֶׁת נָבָ֥ל הַֽכַּרְמְלִֽי׃
records.gloss: And [the] two wives of David had been taken captive, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail [the] wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
pieces: David's two wives had been taken captive too: Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail, the widow of Nabal of Carmel.

L.5: And the two wives of David had been taken captive, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

R.5: David's two wives had also been taken: Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, and Abigail, whose first husband Nabal had come from Carmel.

decisions.choice: Ahinoam the Jezreelite, Abigail of Nabal the Carmelite: David's two wives, both from Judah
decisions.reason: David married both women while he was a fugitive (25:42-43; 27:3). Jezreel here is a town in the hill country of Judah (Joshua 15:56), not the better-known Jezreel in the north. Carmel is a town south of Hebron (25:2), not Mount Carmel.

decisions.choice: the wife of Nabal: Nabal's widow
decisions.reason: Nabal had died (25:38-39), and David then married Abigail. She is still named by her first husband, as she is in 27:3.

decisions.choice: the widow of Nabal; whose first husband Nabal
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that Nabal was dead (m2), so the reader does not think Abigail had two living husbands.

records.source: וַתֵּ֨צֶר לְדָוִ֜ד מְאֹ֗ד כִּֽי־אָמְר֤וּ הָעָם֙ לְסָקְל֔וֹ כִּֽי־מָ֨רָה֙ נֶ֣פֶשׁ כָּל־הָעָ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ עַל־בָּנָ֣יו וְעַל־בְּנֹתָ֑יו וַיִּתְחַזֵּ֣ק דָּוִ֔ד בַּיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהָֽיו׃ס
records.gloss: And it was distressing to David greatly, for said the people to stone him, for was bitter [the] soul of all the people, each over his sons and over his daughters; and strengthened himself David in Yahweh his God.
pieces: David was in deep distress, because the troops were talking about stoning him. Each of them was bitter over his sons and daughters. Yet David drew strength from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God.

L.6: And David was in great distress, for the people spoke of stoning him, for the soul of all the people was bitter, each man over his sons and over his daughters. But David strengthened himself in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God.

R.6: David was in great trouble, because his soldiers were talking about killing him by throwing stones at him. They were all full of grief and anger over their lost sons and daughters. But David found new courage in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God.

decisions.choice: David was in great distress: hemmed in, by grief and by danger
decisions.reason: The verb means to be narrow or tight, to be pressed on every side. David has lost his own family, and now his own men turn on him.

decisions.choice: the soul of all the people was bitter: grief mixed with anger
decisions.reason: Bitterness of soul is deep grief that can turn to anger (1:10 of Hannah; 22:2; Judges 18:25). The men blame David for leaving the town unguarded.

decisions.choice: spoke of stoning him: a mob ready to kill its leader
decisions.reason: Stoning was the way a crowd put someone to death (Exodus 17:4, where the people are about to stone Moses; Numbers 14:10).

decisions.choice: David strengthened himself in the LORD his God: he took courage from the LORD
decisions.reason: The verb means to make oneself strong or firm. David's strength comes from the LORD whom he calls his God, and he turns at once to ask the LORD what to do (verses 7-8). Saul, at the same time, finds no answer from the LORD (28:6).

decisions.choice: drew strength (Balanced), found new courage (Readable)
decisions.reason: The reflexive "strengthened himself" is put as finding strength or courage, which is what it means in this setting.

decisions.choice: full of grief and anger
decisions.reason: Readable explains "bitter of soul" (m2) instead of keeping the picture.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד אֶל־אֶבְיָתָ֤ר הַכֹּהֵן֙ בֶּן־אֲחִימֶ֔לֶךְ הַגִּֽישָׁה־נָּ֥א לִ֖י הָאֵפֹ֑ד וַיַּגֵּ֧שׁ אֶבְיָתָ֛ר אֶת־הָאֵפֹ֖ד אֶל־דָּוִֽד׃
records.gloss: And said David to Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech, Bring near please to me the ephod. And brought near Abiathar the ephod to David.
pieces: David told Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech's son, "Bring the ephod here to me, please." So Abiathar brought the ephod to David.

L.7: And David said to Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech, "Bring the ephod near to me, please." And Abiathar brought the ephod near to David.

R.7: David said to Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech's son, "Please bring me the ephod." The ephod was the priest's vest used to ask God for answers. Abiathar brought it to David.

decisions.choice: Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech: the one priest who escaped Saul's killing at Nob
decisions.reason: Saul had the priests of Nob put to death for helping David. Only Abiathar escaped and fled to David (22:20-23), and he brought an ephod with him (23:6).

decisions.choice: bring the ephod near: bring the priestly garment used to ask God's answer
decisions.reason: The ephod held the breastpiece with the Urim and Thummim, by which the LORD's will was asked (Exodus 28:6-30; Numbers 27:21; see 14:3). David asks through it here, as he did at Keilah (23:9-12).

decisions.choice: The ephod was the priest's vest used to ask God for answers.
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word, as at 14:3.

records.heading: David pursues the raiders

records.source: וַיִּשְׁאַ֨ל דָּוִ֤ד בַּֽיהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אֶרְדֹּ֛ף אַחֲרֵ֥י הַגְּדוּד־הַזֶּ֖ה הַֽאַשִּׂגֶ֑נּוּ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ רְדֹ֔ף כִּֽי־הַשֵּׂ֥ג תַּשִּׂ֖יג וְהַצֵּ֥ל תַּצִּֽיל׃
records.gloss: And inquired David of Yahweh, saying, Shall I pursue after the band the this? Will I overtake it? And he said to him, Pursue, for overtaking you will overtake and rescuing you will rescue.
pieces: Then David inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Should I go after this raiding party? Will I catch up with them?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered him, "Go after them. You will certainly catch up with them, and you will certainly rescue the captives."

L.8: And David inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "Shall I pursue after this band? Will I overtake it?" And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "Pursue, for you will surely overtake [them], and you will surely rescue [them]."

R.8: David asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Should I chase these raiders? Will I catch them?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "Chase them. You will surely catch them, and you will surely save the people they took."

decisions.choice: two questions that can be answered yes or no
decisions.reason: Asking the LORD through the ephod gave answers of this kind, so David puts his questions in that form (14:37; 23:11-12). The answer meets both questions: "Pursue" answers the first, and the promise answers the second.

decisions.choice: the band: a raiding troop that strikes and withdraws
decisions.reason: The word names a band of raiders rather than a regular army (verses 15, 23; 2 Samuel 3:22).

decisions.choice: overtaking you will overtake, rescuing you will rescue: a certain promise
decisions.reason: Each verb is doubled for emphasis: David will certainly catch up and certainly rescue. "Rescue" has no object here; it covers the captives and the goods, as verses 18-19 show.

decisions.choice: he said, with a deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The one who answers is the LORD, so the pronoun takes the reader setting for pronouns referring to God.

decisions.choice: The LORD answered; the captives / the people they took
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker and say what will be rescued (m3).

records.source: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֗ד ה֚וּאוְשֵׁשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת אִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ עַד־נַ֣חַל הַבְּשׂ֑וֹר וְהַנּֽוֹתָרִ֖ים עָמָֽדוּ׃
records.gloss: And went David, he and six hundred men who [were] with him, and they came to [the] wadi of the Besor, and those left behind stayed.
pieces: So David set out with the 600 men who were with him. They came to the Wadi Besor, where those who were left behind stayed.

L.9: And David went, he and the 600 men who [were] with him, and they came to the Wadi Besor, and those left behind stayed [there].

R.9: So David left with his 600 men. They came to the Besor Valley. Some of the men stayed there.

decisions.choice: the Wadi Besor: a streambed south of Ziklag
decisions.reason: A wadi is a valley with a stream that runs only in the rainy season. The Besor runs from the Negev to the sea south of Gaza, and its banks are steep in places, which is why crossing it was hard for tired men (verse 10).

decisions.choice: those left behind stayed: a first word about what verse 10 tells in full
decisions.reason: The narrator mentions the men who stayed at the wadi before explaining who they were and why they stayed.

decisions.choice: the Besor Valley
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word for the dry streambed (m1).

records.source: וַיִּרְדֹּ֣ף דָּוִ֔ד ה֖וּא וְאַרְבַּע־מֵא֣וֹת אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּֽעַמְדוּ֙ מָאתַ֣יִם אִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פִּגְּר֔וּ מֵעֲבֹ֖ר אֶת־נַ֥חַל הַבְּשֽׂוֹר׃
records.gloss: And pursued David, he and four hundred man, and stayed two hundred man who were exhausted from crossing the wadi of the Besor.
pieces: David and 400 men kept up the pursuit, while 200 men stayed behind, too exhausted to cross the Wadi Besor.

L.10: And David pursued, he and 400 men, and 200 men who were too exhausted to cross the Wadi Besor stayed [behind].

R.10: David and 400 men kept chasing the Amalekites. But 200 men were too tired to cross the valley, so they stayed behind.

decisions.choice: exhausted: too worn out to go on
decisions.reason: The verb is found only here and in verse 21. From the setting it means to be faint or spent. The men had marched for three days from Aphek (verse 1) and then wept until they had no strength left (verse 4).

decisions.choice: he and 400 men: David goes on with two thirds of his force
decisions.reason: The 600 of verse 9 are now divided: 400 go on, 200 stay. Verses 21-25 turn on the share of these 200.

decisions.choice: chasing the Amalekites
decisions.reason: Readable names whom David was pursuing.

records.source: וַֽיִּמְצְא֤וּ אִישׁ־מִצְרִי֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה וַיִּקְח֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ אֶל־דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּתְּנוּ־ל֥וֹ לֶ֨חֶם֙ וַיֹּ֔אכַל וַיַּשְׁקֻ֖הוּ מָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And they found a man, Egyptian, in the field, and they took him to David, and they gave to him bread and he ate, and they gave him to drink water.
pieces: They found an Egyptian out in the open country and brought him to David. They gave him food to eat and water to drink.

L.11: And they found an Egyptian man in the open country, and they took him to David, and they gave him bread and he ate, and they gave him water to drink.

R.11: David's men found a man from Egypt out in the fields. They brought him to David. They gave him some bread to eat and water to drink.

decisions.choice: in the field: out in the open country
decisions.reason: The word means open land away from towns, whether pasture, farmland or wild ground.

decisions.choice: bread: food
decisions.reason: The word means bread and often food in general (verse 12).

decisions.choice: David's men
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are.

records.source: וַיִּתְּנוּ־לוֹ֩ פֶ֨לַח דְּבֵלָ֜ה וּשְׁנֵ֤י צִמֻּקִים֙ וַיֹּ֔אכַל וַתָּ֥שָׁב רוּח֖וֹ אֵלָ֑יו כִּ֠י לֹֽא־אָ֤כַל לֶ֨חֶם֙ וְלֹא־שָׁ֣תָה מַ֔יִם שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה יָמִ֖ים וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה לֵילֽוֹת׃ס
records.gloss: And they gave to him a piece of fig cake and two clusters of raisins, and he ate, and returned his spirit to him, for not he had eaten bread and not he had drunk water three days and three nights.
pieces: They also gave him a piece of pressed fig cake and two clusters of raisins. When he had eaten, his strength came back, for he had had no food or water for three days and three nights.

L.12: And they gave him a piece of fig cake and two clusters of raisins, and he ate, and his spirit returned to him, for he had not eaten bread or drunk water for three days and three nights.

R.12: They gave him part of a cake of dried figs and two bunches of raisins. After he ate, he felt strong again. He had not eaten any food or drunk any water for three whole days and nights.

decisions.choice: fig cake and clusters of raisins: dried fruit pressed for travel
decisions.reason: Figs were pressed into cakes and grapes dried in clusters, food that kept and could be carried. Abigail brought the same things to David (25:18).

decisions.choice: his spirit returned to him: his strength and alertness came back
decisions.reason: "Spirit" here is breath and life-force. The same phrase is used of Samson when he drinks after the battle (Judges 15:19).

decisions.choice: his strength came back; he felt strong again
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m2).

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר ל֤וֹ דָוִד֙ לְֽמִי־אַ֔תָּה וְאֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה אָ֑תָּה וַיֹּ֜אמֶר נַ֧עַר מִצְרִ֣י אָנֹ֗כִי עֶ֚בֶד לְאִ֣ישׁ עֲמָֽלֵקִ֔י וַיַּעַזְבֵ֧נִי אֲדֹנִ֛י כִּ֥י חָלִ֖יתִי הַיּ֥וֹם שְׁלֹשָֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And said to him David, To whom [are] you, and where from this [are] you? And he said, [A] young man, Egyptian, [am] I, [a] slave of a man, Amalekite, and abandoned me my master, for I was sick the day three.
pieces: David asked him, "Who do you belong to, and where are you from?" He answered, "I am a young Egyptian, the servant of an Amalekite. My master left me behind three days ago because I fell sick.

L.13: And David said to him, "To whom [do] you [belong], and where [are] you from?" And he said, "I [am] a young Egyptian man, [the] slave of an Amalekite man, and my master abandoned me, because I fell sick three days ago.

R.13: David asked him, "Who is your master? Where are you from?" He said, "I am from Egypt. I am the servant of an Amalekite man. Three days ago I got sick, so my master left me behind.

decisions.choice: to whom are you: whose man are you
decisions.reason: The question asks whom he belongs to: his master, his clan or his people. His answer names both his people and his master.

decisions.choice: slave of an Amalekite: owned, and abandoned when he was no longer useful
decisions.reason: He was not hired but owned, and his master left him to die when he fell sick and could not keep up with the raiders.

decisions.choice: the day three: three days ago
decisions.reason: Counting the present day, this means the day before yesterday, which fits the three days and nights he had gone without food (verse 12).

decisions.choice: servant (Balanced and Readable); slave (Literal)
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for this word: Literal keeps "slave"; Balanced and Readable say "servant", while m2 keeps the fact that he was owned.

records.source: אֲנַ֡חְנוּ פָּשַׁ֜טְנוּ נֶ֧גֶב הַכְּרֵתִ֛י וְעַל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִֽיהוּדָ֖ה וְעַל־נֶ֣גֶב כָּלֵ֑ב וְאֶת־צִקְלַ֖ג שָׂרַ֥פְנוּ בָאֵֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: We, we raided [the] Negev of the Cherethites and against what [belongs] to Judah and against [the] Negev of Caleb, and Ziklag we burned with fire.
pieces: We raided the Negev of the Cherethites, the part that belongs to Judah, and the Negev of Caleb, and we burned Ziklag down."

L.14: We made a raid [on the] Negev of the Cherethites, and on what [belongs] to Judah, and on [the] Negev of Caleb, and we burned Ziklag with fire."

R.14: We made raids in the south, on the land of the Cherethites, the land of Judah, and the land of Caleb's people. And we burned Ziklag."

decisions.choice: the Negev of the Cherethites: southern land held by a people linked with the Philistines
decisions.reason: The Cherethites lived near the Philistines on the southern coast (Ezekiel 25:16; Zephaniah 2:5) and probably came from Crete. Later some of them served as David's guard (2 Samuel 8:18).

decisions.choice: what belongs to Judah: the Negev of Judah
decisions.reason: The phrase stands for the southern land of Judah, which David named in his reports to Achish (27:10).

decisions.choice: the Negev of Caleb: the southern land of the clan of Caleb
decisions.reason: Caleb was given Hebron and the land around it (Joshua 14:13; 15:13), and his clan lived there and to the south. Nabal was a Calebite (25:3).

decisions.choice: the land of ...; Caleb's people
decisions.reason: Readable says "the south" once and then "the land of" for each part, and makes clear that Caleb here means his clan.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ דָּוִ֔ד הֲתוֹרִדֵ֖נִי אֶל־הַגְּד֣וּד הַזֶּ֑ה וַיֹּ֡אמֶר הִשָּׁבְעָה֩ לִּ֨י בֵֽאלֹהִ֜ים אִם־תְּמִיתֵ֗נִי וְאִם־תַּסְגִּרֵ֨נִי֙ בְּיַד־אֲדֹנִ֔י וְאוֹרִֽדְךָ֖ אֶל־הַגְּד֥וּד הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And said to him David, Will you bring me down to the band the this? And he said, Swear to me by God, if you will kill me and if you will deliver me into [the] hand of my master, and I will bring you down to the band the this.
pieces: David asked him, "Will you lead me down to this raiding party?" He replied, "Give me your oath by God that you will neither kill me nor hand me over to my master, and I will take you down to them."

L.15: And David said to him, "Will you take me down to this band?" And he said, "Swear to me by God that you will not kill me and will not hand me over into the hand of my master, and I will take you down to this band."

R.15: David asked, "Can you lead me to these raiders?" He answered, "Promise me in God's name that you will not kill me or give me back to my master. Then I will take you to them."

decisions.choice: swear ... if you kill me: swear that you will not kill me
decisions.reason: In an oath, "if" with no second half means "certainly not": "may it happen to me if I do." So he asks for a promise that David will neither kill him nor return him.

decisions.choice: swear by God: an oath in the name of God
decisions.reason: The Egyptian uses the general word for God, not the LORD's name. An oath in God's name bound the one who swore before God.

decisions.choice: deliver into the hand of my master: hand me over to his power
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power or control. A runaway slave returned to his master could expect harsh treatment.

decisions.choice: to them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable avoid repeating "this band" at the end of the sentence.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣רִדֵ֔הוּ וְהִנֵּ֥ה נְטֻשִׁ֖ים עַל־פְּנֵ֣י כָל־הָאָ֑רֶץ אֹכְלִ֤ים וְשֹׁתִים֙ וְחֹ֣גְגִ֔ים בְּכֹל֙ הַשָּׁלָ֣ל הַגָּד֔וֹל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָקְח֛וּ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים וּמֵאֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he brought him down, and there! [they were] spread out over [the] face of all the land, eating and drinking and celebrating, because of all the plunder the great which they had taken from [the] land of [the] Philistines and from [the] land of Judah.
pieces: So he led him down, and there they were, spread out over the whole area, eating and drinking and celebrating over all the great plunder they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.

L.16: And he took him down, and look, they [were] spread out over the face of all the land, eating and drinking and celebrating, because of all the great plunder that they had taken from the land of [the] Philistines and from the land of Judah.

R.16: So the Egyptian led David down to them. The Amalekites were scattered all over the place. They were eating and drinking and having a party. They were celebrating all the things they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from Judah.

decisions.choice: look, spread out: the raiders scattered and off guard
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, "look" shows the scene as the newcomers saw it. The raiders were spread over the whole area, not set in any guarded camp. They thought themselves safe, which gave David his chance.

decisions.choice: celebrating: feasting as at a festival, with dancing
decisions.reason: The verb is used for keeping a religious festival, and for dancing and making merry (Exodus 5:1, of holding a festival to the LORD in the wilderness).

decisions.choice: plunder from the land of the Philistines and of Judah
decisions.reason: The raid struck both peoples while their armies were away in the north at Aphek (29:1). The plunder from the Philistines is the reason David can later send some to Judah (verse 26).

decisions.choice: the Egyptian, David, the Amalekites
decisions.reason: Readable names the people behind each "he" and "they".

records.source: וַיַּכֵּ֥ם דָּוִ֛ד מֵהַנֶּ֥שֶׁף וְעַד־הָעֶ֖רֶב לְמָֽחֳרָתָ֑ם וְלֹֽא־נִמְלַ֤ט מֵהֶם֙ אִ֔ישׁ כִּי֩ אִם־אַרְבַּ֨ע מֵא֧וֹת אִֽישׁ־נַ֛עַר אֲשֶׁר־רָכְב֥וּ עַל־הַגְּמַלִּ֖ים וַיָּנֻֽסוּ׃
records.gloss: And struck them David from the twilight and until the evening of their next day, and not escaped of them a man, except four hundred man [of] young men who rode on the camels and fled.
pieces: From twilight until the evening of the following day David struck them down. Not one of them escaped except 400 young men, who got on camels and fled.

L.17: And David struck them from the twilight until the evening of their next day, and not a man of them escaped, except 400 young men who rode on the camels and fled.

R.17: David attacked them from twilight until the evening of the next day. None of them got away except 400 young men. They got on camels and rode away.

decisions.choice: from the twilight until the evening of the next day: a fight lasting about a day
alternatives: from dawn until the evening of the next day
decisions.reason: The word for twilight is used both of the half-light of evening (Isaiah 5:11) and of dawn (Job 7:4). If it is evening twilight here, David attacked at dusk and fought until the next evening; if dawn, he attacked at first light and fought until the following evening. "Their next day" means the day after for the Amalekites.

decisions.choice: rode on the camels and fled: desert raiders escaping on fast mounts
decisions.reason: Desert raiders such as the Amalekites and Midianites came on camels (Judges 6:5; 7:12), and camels could outrun men on foot. The 400 who escape match the 400 men with David.

decisions.choice: twilight
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep "twilight", which, like the Hebrew word, can be evening or morning (m1).

records.source: וַיַּצֵּ֣ל דָּוִ֔ד אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָקְח֖וּ עֲמָלֵ֑ק וְאֶת־שְׁתֵּ֥י נָשָׁ֖יו הִצִּ֥יל דָּוִֽד׃
records.gloss: And rescued David all that had taken Amalek, and his two wives rescued David.
pieces: David recovered everything the Amalekites had taken, and he rescued his two wives.

L.18: And David rescued all that Amalek had taken, and David rescued his two wives.

R.18: David got back everything the Amalekites had taken. He also rescued his two wives.

decisions.choice: rescued: snatched back, recovered
decisions.reason: The verb means to snatch someone or something out of another's power. It is the word of the LORD's promise in verse 8, now kept.

decisions.choice: Amalek: the people of Amalek
decisions.reason: The name of the ancestor stands for the whole people (15:2-3; Exodus 17:8).

decisions.choice: his two wives David rescued: the wives named for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "his two wives" first in its clause, giving weight to the rescue of the women named in verse 5.

decisions.choice: the Amalekites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the name of the people (m2).

records.source: וְלֹ֣א נֶעְדַּר־לָ֠הֶם מִן־הַקָּטֹ֨ן וְעַד־הַגָּד֜וֹל וְעַד־בָּנִ֤ים וּבָנוֹת֙ וּמִשָּׁלָ֔ל וְעַ֛ד כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָקְח֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם הַכֹּ֖ל הֵשִׁ֥יב דָּוִֽד׃
records.gloss: And not was missing to them from the small and unto the great and unto sons and daughters and from plunder and unto all that they had taken for themselves; the all brought back David.
pieces: Nothing of theirs was missing, small or great, sons or daughters, plunder or anything else the raiders had taken. David brought it all back.

L.19: And nothing of theirs was missing, from the small to the great, to sons and daughters, and from [the] plunder to all that they had taken for themselves; David brought back everything.

R.19: Nothing was missing, large or small. David brought back every son and daughter, and everything else the raiders had taken.

decisions.choice: from the small to the great: everything, of every kind
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, the pair means "all of it". Here it covers people and goods alike, and the list goes on to children and plunder.

decisions.choice: nothing missing; David brought back everything
decisions.reason: The verse stresses that the promise of verse 8 was kept in full: the LORD had said David would rescue, and not one person or thing was lost.

decisions.choice: the raiders
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who "they" are, since "they" in the first clause are David's men.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֣ח דָּוִ֔ד אֶת־כָּל־הַצֹּ֖אן וְהַבָּקָ֑ר נָהֲג֗וּ לִפְנֵי֙ הַמִּקְנֶ֣ה הַה֔וּא וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ זֶ֖ה שְׁלַ֥ל דָּוִֽד׃
records.gloss: And took David all the flocks and the herds; they drove before the livestock the that, and they said, This [is the] plunder of David.
pieces: David also took all the flocks and herds. His men drove them ahead of the other livestock and said, "This is David's plunder."

L.20: And David took all the flocks and the herds; they drove [them] before that livestock, and they said, "This [is] David's plunder."

R.20: David also took all the Amalekites' sheep and cattle. His men drove these animals in front of the others and said, "This is David's plunder!"

decisions.choice: David took the Amalekites' own flocks and herds; the men drove them ahead of the recovered animals
alternatives: the men drove all the livestock in front of David and said, "This is David's plunder"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is brief and hard to follow. The most likely sense is that, besides recovering what had been taken from Ziklag, David took the raiders' own flocks and herds, and his men drove these in front of the other livestock as David's prize. Another way to read it is that the men drove all the animals in front of David, calling the whole herd his plunder.

decisions.choice: This is David's plunder: the men honor David as their leader
decisions.reason: The cry gives the credit for the victory to David. In verse 26 David gives part of this plunder away to the elders of Judah.

decisions.choice: His men; the other livestock; the Amalekites' (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who drove the animals and which animals, following m1.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֣א דָוִ֗ד אֶל־מָאתַ֨יִם הָאֲנָשִׁ֜ים אֲשֶֽׁר־פִּגְּר֣וּ׀מִלֶּ֣כֶת׀אַחֲרֵ֣י דָוִ֗ד וַיֹּֽשִׁיבֻם֙ בְּנַ֣חַל הַבְּשׂ֔וֹר וַיֵּֽצְאוּ֙ לִקְרַ֣את דָּוִ֔ד וְלִקְרַ֖את הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֑וֹ וַיִּגַּ֤שׁ דָּוִד֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם וַיִּשְׁאַ֥ל לָהֶ֖ם לְשָׁלֽוֹם׃ס
records.gloss: And came David to [the] two hundred the men who had been exhausted from going after David, and they had made them stay at [the] wadi of the Besor, and they went out to meet David and to meet the people who [were] with him; and approached David the people and asked them of peace.
pieces: Then David came back to the 200 men who had been too exhausted to follow him and had been left at the Wadi Besor. They came out to meet David and the troops with him, and as David came near, he greeted them.

L.21: And David came to the 200 men who had been too exhausted to go after David, whom they had left at the Wadi Besor; and they went out to meet David and to meet the people who [were] with him. And David approached the people and asked them about [their] well-being.

R.21: David came back to the 200 men who had been too tired to go with him. They had stayed at the Besor Valley. They came out to meet David and the soldiers with him. David went up to them and greeted them warmly.

decisions.choice: asked them of peace: greeted them, asking how they were
decisions.reason: To "ask someone about peace" is the usual greeting, asking after their welfare (17:22; 25:5). David meets the men who stayed behind as friends, not as failures.

decisions.choice: they had made them stay: the 200 had been left behind by the others
decisions.reason: The verb means "caused to stay". The subject is not named; it is David's party, who left the exhausted men at the wadi (verses 9-10).

decisions.choice: the people: the 400 with David, then the 200 at the wadi
decisions.reason: The first "people" are David's 400 fighting men; the second time, "the people" David comes near to are the 200 who come out to meet him.

decisions.choice: troops (Balanced), soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 4.

decisions.choice: greeted them warmly
decisions.reason: Readable adds "warmly" to give the sense of asking after their welfare (m1).

records.source: וַיַּ֜עַן כָּל־אִֽישׁ־רָ֣ע וּבְלִיַּ֗עַל מֵֽהָאֲנָשִׁים֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָלְכ֣וּ עִם־דָּוִד֒ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ יַ֚עַן אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־הָלְכ֣וּ עִמִּ֔י לֹֽא־נִתֵּ֣ן לָהֶ֔ם מֵהַשָּׁלָ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִצַּ֑לְנוּ כִּֽי־אִם־אִ֤ישׁ אֶת־אִשְׁתּוֹ֙ וְאֶת־בָּנָ֔יו וְיִנְהֲג֖וּ וְיֵלֵֽכוּ׃ס
records.gloss: And answered every man evil and worthless of the men who had gone with David, and they said, Because that not they went with me, not we will give to them of the plunder which we have rescued, except each his wife and his children, and let them drive [them] off and go.
pieces: But every wicked and worthless man in the company that had gone with David said, "Since they did not go with us, we will not give them any of the plunder we recovered. Each man may take his wife and {{gender:children|sons}} and go."

L.22: And every evil and worthless man among the men who had gone with David answered and said, "Because they did not go with me, we will not give them [any] of the plunder that we have recovered, except to each man his wife and his {{gender:children|sons}}; let them lead [them] away and go."

R.22: But the evil troublemakers among the men who had gone with David said, "These men did not go with us. So we will not give them any of the things we got back. Each of them can take his wife and {{gender:children|sons}} and leave."

decisions.choice: evil and worthless men: wicked men who reject what is right
decisions.reason: The word for "worthless" is the one used of Eli's sons (2:12), of those who despised Saul (10:27) and of Nabal (25:17, 25). "Every evil and worthless man" means all the men of that kind, not the whole 400.

decisions.choice: they did not go with me: the group speaks as one man
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "with me", as though each man spoke for himself or the group spoke with one voice. The ancient Greek translation reads "with us". The sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: his wife and his children; let them drive them off and go
decisions.reason: The word for "sons" here means children of both sexes, as in verse 19. "Drive off" is the verb of verse 2: the men may lead their families away but get nothing else.

decisions.choice: with us
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural for a group speaking together (m2).

records.heading: Equal shares for those who stayed behind

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד לֹֽא־תַעֲשׂ֥וּ כֵ֖ן אֶחָ֑י אֵ֠ת אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה לָ֨נוּ֙ וַיִּשְׁמֹ֣ר אֹתָ֔נוּ וַיִּתֵּ֗ן אֶֽת־הַגְּד֛וּד הַבָּ֥א עָלֵ֖ינוּ בְּיָדֵֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And said David, Not you shall do so, my brothers, with what has given Yahweh to us; and he has kept us and has given the band that came against us into our hand.
pieces: But David said, "My brothers, you must not act this way with what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given us. He has kept us safe and has handed over to us the raiding party that came against us.

L.23: But David said, "You shall not do so, my brothers, with what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given us. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has kept us and has given the band that came against us into our hand.

R.23: But David said, "My brothers, you must not do this. These things are what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given us. He kept us safe, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave us victory over the raiders who attacked us.

decisions.choice: what the LORD has given us: the plunder is the LORD's gift, not the fighters' own winnings
decisions.reason: David answers that the plunder was not won by the strength of the 400. The LORD kept them alive and gave them the victory, so no one may claim it by right of his own effort.

decisions.choice: has given the band into our hand: has given us victory over them
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power. To give an enemy into someone's hand is to let them defeat it (14:10; 23:4).

decisions.choice: my brothers: comrades
decisions.reason: David speaks to his men as fellow members of one company, not as their master. These are the men who wanted to stone him (verse 6).

decisions.choice: he, with a deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The one who kept them and gave them victory is the LORD, so a pronoun for him inside a sentence takes the reader setting.

decisions.choice: gave us victory over
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m2).

records.source: וּמִי֙ יִשְׁמַ֣ע לָכֶ֔ם לַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֞י כְּחֵ֣לֶק׀הַיֹּרֵ֣ד בַּמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וּֽכְחֵ֛לֶק הַיֹּשֵׁ֥ב עַל־הַכֵּלִ֖ים יַחְדָּ֥ו יַחֲלֹֽקוּ׃ס
records.gloss: And who will listen to you in the matter the this? For as [the] share of the [one] going down into the battle, and as [the] share of the [one] staying by the baggage, together they shall share.
pieces: Who would listen to you in this matter? The share of the man who stays with the supplies is to be the same as the share of the man who goes down into battle. They will share alike."

L.24: And who will listen to you in this matter? For as [is] the share of the one going down into the battle, so [is] the share of the one staying by the baggage; they shall share alike."

R.24: No one will agree with you about this! The man who stays behind to guard the supplies will get the same share as the man who goes into battle. Everyone will share alike."

decisions.choice: who will listen to you: a question that means no one will
decisions.reason: David's question expects the answer "no one": no one in Israel would accept the rule the worthless men propose.

decisions.choice: the one staying by the baggage: the man who guards the supplies
decisions.reason: The word means gear, equipment and supplies. Guarding them was a real duty in war (17:22; 25:13, where David leaves 200 men with the baggage).

decisions.choice: they shall share alike: one rule for those who fought and those who stayed
decisions.reason: The plunder from Midian was divided in a similar way between the fighters and the rest of the congregation (Numbers 31:27), and Joshua told the tribes going home to share their plunder with their brothers (Joshua 22:8). Verse 25 makes David's rule lasting law.

decisions.choice: the share of the man who stays ... the same as the share of the man who goes
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the man who stayed first, since he is the one whose share was in question; the meaning of the comparison is unchanged.

decisions.choice: No one will agree with you about this!
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies (m1).

records.source: וַיְהִ֕י מֵֽהַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וָמָ֑עְלָה וַיְשִׂמֶ֜הָ לְחֹ֤ק וּלְמִשְׁפָּט֙ לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And it was from the day the that and onward, and he set it as a statute and as a judgment for Israel until the day the this.
pieces: From that day on it was so: David made it a statute and a ruling for Israel, and it remains so to this day.

L.25: And it was [so] from that day and onward; and he made it a statute and a judgment for Israel, to this day.

R.25: From that day on, David made this a law and a rule for Israel. It is still the rule to this day.

decisions.choice: a statute and a judgment: a fixed rule and a binding decision
decisions.reason: The two words are often paired for the laws of Israel (Exodus 15:25; Joshua 24:25). The first means something fixed or set down; the second, a ruling that decides cases. Together they say that David's decision became the standing law for sharing plunder.

decisions.choice: he made it: David
decisions.reason: The subject is David. Before he is king he already acts as a ruler who sets law for Israel.

decisions.choice: to this day: up to the time the account was written
decisions.reason: As at 5:5, the phrase refers to the writer's own day, when the rule was still kept.

decisions.choice: David
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject (m2).

decisions.choice: a statute and a ruling (Balanced); a law and a rule (Readable)
decisions.reason: The pair follows the wording set for these two words: "statutes and judgments" at Literal, "statutes and rulings" at Balanced, "laws and rules" at Readable, here in the singular.

records.gloss: And came David to Ziklag, and he sent of the plunder to [the] elders of Judah, to his friends, saying, Here, for you [is] a blessing from [the] plunder of [the] enemies of Yahweh,
pieces: Back in Ziklag, David sent part of the plunder to the elders of Judah, who were his friends, with the words, "Here is a gift for you, taken from the plunder of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s enemies."

L.26: And David came to Ziklag, and he sent some of the plunder to the elders of Judah, to his friends, saying, "Here [is] a blessing for you from the plunder of the enemies of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}",

R.26: When David got back to Ziklag, he sent some of the things they had taken to his friends, the elders of Judah. He told them, "Here is a gift for you. It comes from what we took from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s enemies."

decisions.choice: a blessing: a gift given as a sign of goodwill
decisions.reason: A gift that carries good wishes is called a "blessing" (25:27, of Abigail's gift to David; Genesis 33:11).

decisions.choice: the enemies of the LORD: Amalek, the LORD's enemy since the exodus
decisions.reason: The LORD had sworn to war against Amalek (Exodus 17:14-16; 15:2-3). David presents the plunder as won in the LORD's war, a share in the LORD's victory.

decisions.choice: the elders of Judah, his friends: leaders of the towns of his own tribe
decisions.reason: The elders led the towns and clans. Most of the towns in verses 27-31 lie in the south of Judah, where David had moved about while he fled from Saul and where he had raided the enemies of Judah (27:8-10). Soon after, the men of Judah make him king at Hebron (2 Samuel 2:1-4).

decisions.choice: to his friends: the same people as the elders
decisions.reason: The phrase stands next to "the elders of Judah" and names them again. The ancient Greek translation reads "and to his friends", as if these were a second group.

decisions.choice: a gift
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "gift" for "blessing" in this sense (m1).

records.heading: Gifts to the elders of Judah

records.source: לַאֲשֶׁ֧ר בְּבֵֽית־אֵ֛ל וְלַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּרָמֽוֹת־נֶ֖גֶב וְלַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּיַתִּֽר׃
records.gloss: to those who [were] in Bethel and to those who [were] in Ramoth of [the] Negev and to those who [were] in Jattir,
pieces: He sent it to those in Bethel, in Ramoth of the Negev and in Jattir,

L.27: to those who [were] in Bethel, and to those who [were] in Ramoth of the Negev, and to those who [were] in Jattir,

R.27: He sent gifts to the people in the towns of Bethel, Ramoth in the Negev and Jattir.

decisions.choice: Bethel: a town in the south of Judah, not the Bethel north of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The well-known Bethel lay in the north, far from the others in this list. A southern town called Bethul or Bethuel was in the land of Simeon (Joshua 19:4; 1 Chronicles 4:30), and the name here probably means that town. The ancient Greek translation reads Beth-zur, a town north of Hebron.

decisions.choice: Ramoth of the Negev; Jattir: towns in the south of Judah
decisions.reason: Ramoth of the Negev is probably the "Ramah of the Negev" in Simeon's land (Joshua 19:8). Jattir was a town in the hill country south of Hebron, later given to the priests (Joshua 15:48; 21:14).

decisions.choice: He sent it / He sent gifts
decisions.reason: The list continues the sentence begun in verse 26. Balanced and Readable start it again with "He sent", since the quotation stands between.

decisions.choice: one sentence for each verse of the list
decisions.reason: Readable gives each verse of the list its own short sentence (verses 27-31).

records.gloss: and to those who [were] in Aroer and to those who [were] in Siphmoth and to those who [were] in Eshtemoa,
pieces: to those in Aroer, in Siphmoth and in Eshtemoa,

L.28: and to those who [were] in Aroer, and to those who [were] in Siphmoth, and to those who [were] in Eshtemoa,

R.28: He sent gifts to the people in Aroer, Siphmoth and Eshtemoa.

decisions.choice: Aroer, Siphmoth, Eshtemoa: towns of the south
decisions.reason: This Aroer is a town of the Negev of Judah, not the Aroer east of the Jordan on the Arnon (Joshua 13:16). Siphmoth is named only here. Eshtemoa lay south of Hebron and was later given to the priests (Joshua 21:14).

decisions.choice: He sent gifts
decisions.reason: As in verse 27.

records.source: וְלַאֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּרָכָ֗ל וְלַֽאֲשֶׁר֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י הַיְּרַחְמְאֵלִ֔י וְלַאֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעָרֵ֥י הַקֵּינִֽי׃
records.gloss: and to those who [were] in Racal and to those who [were] in [the] cities of the Jerahmeelites and to those who [were] in [the] cities of the Kenites,
pieces: to those in Racal, in the towns of the Jerahmeelites and in the towns of the Kenites,

L.29: and to those who [were] in Racal, and to those who [were] in the towns of the Jerahmeelites, and to those who [were] in the towns of the Kenites,

R.29: He sent gifts to the people in Racal, and in the towns of the Jerahmeelites and the Kenites.

decisions.choice: Racal: a town named only here
decisions.reason: Racal is not named elsewhere. The ancient Greek translation reads Carmel, the town of Nabal and Abigail south of Hebron (25:2).

decisions.choice: the Jerahmeelites and the Kenites: clans living in the south of Judah
decisions.reason: The Jerahmeelites were a clan of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:9, 25-27), and the Kenites were the clan linked to Moses by marriage (15:6; Judges 1:16). David had told Achish that he raided these very peoples (27:10); in fact he now sends them gifts.

decisions.choice: He sent gifts
decisions.reason: As in verse 27.

records.gloss: and to those who [were] in Hormah and to those who [were] in Bor-ashan and to those who [were] in Athach,
pieces: to those in Hormah, in Bor-ashan and in Athach,

L.30: and to those who [were] in Hormah, and to those who [were] in Bor-ashan, and to those who [were] in Athach,

R.30: He sent gifts to the people in Hormah, Bor-ashan and Athach.

decisions.choice: Hormah, Bor-ashan, Athach: towns in the land of Simeon and the south of Judah
decisions.reason: Hormah was in the far south (Numbers 21:3; Joshua 19:4). Bor-ashan ("well of Ashan") is probably the Ashan of Joshua 15:42 and 19:7; some Hebrew manuscripts spell its first part with a different letter. Athach is named only here.

decisions.choice: He sent gifts
decisions.reason: As in verse 27.

records.gloss: and to those who [were] in Hebron, and to all the places where had gone about there David, he and his men.
pieces: to those in Hebron, and to all the places where David and his men had moved about.

L.31: and to those who [were] in Hebron, and to all the places where David had gone about, he and his men.

R.31: He also sent gifts to the people in Hebron, and to all the other places where David and his men had stayed.

decisions.choice: Hebron: the chief town of Judah
decisions.reason: Hebron, the old town where Abraham lived and Caleb settled (Genesis 23:2; Joshua 14:13), comes last in the list. David is soon made king there (2 Samuel 2:1-4).

decisions.choice: had gone about: had moved from place to place
decisions.reason: The verb means to walk about or go to and fro. It sums up David's years as a fugitive, when he and his men went wherever they could (23:13).

decisions.choice: had stayed
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain word for the places where David and his men spent time as they moved about.
